UN !VERSITY *


Policy on Anti Ragging

Purlrose and scope of responsibilities:

Ragging is a menace pervading the educational institutions of the country. BML Munjal
University (BMU) believes in inculcating discipline and social integration among its students. In
furtherance of this objective and with the aim of protecting its students from immoral and
inhumane act of'ragging, BMU has adopted BMU Anti- Ragging Policy (ARP) to take care of
preventive, procedural and punitive aspects of ragging. These Regulations are for the purpose of
and by way of implementation of the University Grants Commission Regulations (UGC
Regulations) on curbing the Menace of Ragging in the Higher Educational Institutions, 2oo9.

Ragging is prohibited at BMU and the university shall ensure that:

1. BMU shall make all endeavours to prevent ragging at the institutional level and take
measures to eliminate ragging within BMU and outside. For this prlrpose BMU shall
implement all measures prescribed under Regulation 6 of the UGC Regulations.

2. BMU shall take action in accordance with Regulation 9 of the UGC Regulations against
those found guilty of ragging and/or abetting ragging actively or passively, or being part
of a conspiracy to promote ragging.

Membership:

As per the UGC regulation on curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational

Institutions , 2oog (Under section z6 (r) (g) of the University Grant Commission Act, 1956), the
BMU shall constitute the Anti-Ragging Committee (ARC) and Anti-Ragging Squad (ARS). Below
are the details of membership:

1. The Vice Chancellor shall be the chairperson of the Anti-Ragging Committee (ARC) and
appoint the following other members:

a. One Representative from civil administration ;
b. One Representative from police administration;

One Representative from the local media;
One Representative of NGOs involved in youth activities;
Two Representatives of Faculty members;
One representative of parents;
Two representatives of students;
Two non- teaching staffmembers of the University:

police/local authorities  and such remedial action shall be  initiated  and completed  immediately
and  in  no  case  later  than  a  period  of  seven days  of  the  reported  occurrence  of  the  incident  of
ragging.

BMU shall  on  admission  or  enrolment or  registration  of  freshers:

1.  provide to the  freshers  a  copy of  the  ARP,  informing  them that the  ARP  contains  the
telephone number and email  id  of the z4-hour  Anti-  Ragging  Toll-Free Helpline
established by  the  UGC  to help  students  in  distress  to  get  immediate  assistance;

2.  provide  the  names  and  telephone  numbers  of  the  Vice  Chancellor,  Pro  Vice
Chancellor  (Academic),  members of the ARC and  the  ARS

3.  explain  to  the  freshers  the  arrangements made  for  their induction  and  orientation
which  is  intended  to  promote efficient  and  effective means  of  integrating  the
freshers  fully  as students  with  those already  admitted  to  BMU  in  previous  years;
and

4.  instruct  students  that  they should  desist  from doing  anything,  with  or against  their
will,  even  if  ordered  to  by a  senior student, and  promptly report  any attempt  of
ragging  to  a  member of the  ARS  or  to  the Warden  or  an assistant warden or  to the
Registrar,  Pro Vice  Chancellor  (Academic)  or  Vice Chancellor,  as  the  case  may  be.

5.  obtain  an  affidavit from  every  fresher and  his/her  parents  as  required under  clauses
(d),  (e)  and (g) of Regulation 6.r  of  the  UGC  Regulations  at  the  time  of  admission  or
registration,  as  the  case  may  be,  during  each  year.

6.  shall maintain  a  proper  record  of  the  affidavits and  ensure  its  safe  upkeep  thereof;
including maintaining  the  copies of  the  affidavit  in  an  electronic form,  to  be  accessed
easily  when required.

The  Vice  Chancellor  shall  possess  the  sole  authonty  for  any  interpretation,  modification  or
amendment  to  the  ARP.  The Vice  Chancellor  shall  in  his  discretion  amend  or  repeal  any

clauses  of the ARP  which  the Vice  Chancellor finds unsatisfactory.
